findings.text: The probe receipt is stored on launchArgs but only the one-shot st.launch copies it into launcher.json; the --rounds > 1 branch calls st.repairLoop, whose launcher literal omits Probe, so a passing identity probe is absent from launcher.json on every multi-round run.

Spec item "**cline:** confirm from the vendor CLI reference that a positional prompt runs once and exits (not interactive in a TTY). If it is not confirmable, exclude cline with a reason." is not met: the row comment records yolo mode and the -i TUI flag but never records one-shot exit, while the handed research lists cline's exit as still open, so an interactive CLI can be launched as a headless agent.
findings.quote: // The CLI reference confirms a positional prompt runs in yolo mode; -i opens the TUI.

findings.text: The probe checks the binary resolved in argsFor, but the --rounds path re-resolves the agent in repairLoop and launches through that second path; a PATH change between the two resolutions lets a different binary be launched after a passing probe.
An operator row with probe_match but no probe_args passes closed-key validation and the field is silently ignored, so a misspelled or omitted probe_args leaves the agent unprobed with no refusal.

The kilo probe accepts any output containing the bare word "run"; the same row records a text-editor namesake, whose usage or error text can contain that word, so the wrong binary may pass the identity check.
